body.statement: Under \(\mathrm{ass:uniform\text{-}primitive\text{-}clt}\) and \(\mathrm{ass:uniform\text{-}multiplier\text{-}law}\), determine whether \[n\kappa_n^3\to\infty,\qquad (n\kappa_n)^{-1/2}=o(t_n),\qquad t_n=o(\kappa_n)\] imply uniform simultaneous coverage for the row-feasible schedule-indexed procedure: \[\liminf_{n\to\infty}\inf_{\mathbb P\in\mathfrak P_{\kappa}^{0}}\Pr_{\mathbb P}\!\left\{[L(\beta_n),U(\beta_n)]\subseteq\mathrm{CI}_n(t)\right\}\ge1-\alpha.\] The experiment class \(\mathfrak P_{\kappa}^{0}\) itself imposes none of these rate or tuning conditions.
body.justification: This is the sufficient-regime half of the sole headline frontier for uniform inference with shrinking transportation margins.
body.gap: Cho and Russell provide uniformly valid inference for linear-moment LP functionals through fixed nonvanishing random perturbations, and Gafarov provides uniformly valid sharp-set subvector inference under fixed positive rank and slack constants. Neither theorem establishes validity of this row-feasible numerical-delta procedure under the displayed rare-cell step window.
body.consumer: A positive answer would give a usable tuning regime for simultaneous selector-envelope coverage when deployment and response-study cells become rare.
